title: What is halal?
description: What does halal mean in food? Understand ingredients, label information and the limits of BOTIA’s assessment compared with halal certification.
lead: Halal means permitted under Islamic law. In food, it refers to both ingredients and the conditions in which food is prepared and handled.
food_text: Halal food must come from lawful sources and must not contain pork derivatives, blood or alcohol, which Codex lists among the prohibited sources. An ingredient list can show declared ingredients, but it cannot by itself establish that all Halal requirements are met.
criteria_text: BOTIA marks a label as Halal when no prohibited ingredients or ingredients of doubtful origin are detected in the declared ingredient list.
uncertainty_text: When the label does not establish the origin or process, BOTIA uses Mashbooh (doubt). Missing information is not proof that an ingredient is Halal or Haram.
limits_title: What BOTIA can and cannot conclude
can1: Identify declared ingredients that do not trigger a Haram or Mashbooh classification.
can2: Flag ingredients whose origin or process is unclear instead of assuming they are Halal.
can3: Show which parts of the assessment come directly from the label.
cannot1: Certify that a product is Halal.
cannot2: Verify slaughter methods, manufacturing conditions or cross-contamination when these are not declared.
cannot3: Replace a Halal certification body or religious authority.
